detailed_rationale:
LatentView Analytics is a data-analytics/AI consulting firm serving Technology, BFSI, CPG & Retail, and Industrials clients. Unlike most other names in this batch, the growth story here is genuinely intact and recent: FY26 revenue grew 23% to Rs.1,060 Cr with a healthy 22% operating margin, and Q1 FY27 continued the trend at 21.6% revenue growth with a 20.4% adjusted EBITDA margin -- consistent, multi-quarter, double-digit growth off an already sizeable base, not a base-effect illusion. The balance sheet is close to pristine: debt is minimal (~Rs.33 Cr) and the company is effectively net-cash.

Our own quality score for this name is low (8.6/100), which on its face looks concerning, but the likely driver is capital-efficiency dilution rather than business deterioration: fixed assets jumped from Rs.28 Cr (FY25) to Rs.397 Cr (FY26), a large one-off capex/infrastructure deployment (most likely a campus/office build financed from IPO-era cash) that would mechanically depress ROE (12% 3-year average) even as the operating business performs well -- this is a case where a large, recent, deliberate capital deployment is dragging a return-on-capital-based score down without reflecting deteriorating unit economics. We flag this as our genuine read, not a certainty, since we cannot fully verify the capex's specific purpose from public disclosures reviewed. A new CEO (Sonal Ramrakhiani) took charge effective August 1, 2026 -- a real leadership-transition risk to monitor, and the sector carries the general mid-cap-IT/analytics risks flagged for this space: GenAI-driven pricing pressure on commoditizable analytics work, and client-concentration risk typical of boutique analytics firms.

Reverse-DCF: at ~32x earnings for a business growing revenue at 21-23% with 20%+ EBITDA margins and a net-cash balance sheet, the multiple looks reasonable, arguably undemanding, provided the growth rate holds up against GenAI-driven pricing competition. This is a case where the price does not yet fully credit the demonstrated growth and balance-sheet quality.
recommendation_rationale: We are rescuing the quant Sell to Hold. The quant score's weak read (Sell on the 3-year view driven by a very low 8.6 quality score) appears to be primarily a capital-efficiency artifact from a large, recent, deliberate capex/cash deployment (fixed assets rose 14x in one year) rather than a signal of business deterioration -- the actual operating metrics (21-23% consistent revenue growth, 20-22% margins, net-cash balance sheet) are genuinely healthy and, at ~32x earnings, not expensively priced for that growth. We temper the rescue with real, acknowledged risks: a brand-new CEO and sector-wide GenAI pricing pressure on analytics services, which is why we land at Hold rather than a stronger call.
summary: LatentView Analytics is a data-analytics and AI consulting firm that has delivered consistent 21-23% revenue growth with healthy 20-22% margins and a net-cash balance sheet. Our quantitative score flags this as a Sell, largely because a large one-year jump in fixed assets (likely a facility investment funded from IPO cash) has temporarily depressed capital-efficiency metrics -- but the underlying growth and profitability are genuinely strong, and the ~32x earnings multiple is not demanding for that combination. We are moving this to Hold, while flagging a recent CEO transition and industry-wide GenAI pricing pressure on analytics services as risks to watch.
positive_para: Consistent, multi-quarter double-digit revenue growth (21-23%) off an already-substantial base, healthy and stable operating margins (20-22%), a debt-free/net-cash balance sheet, and a reasonable ~32x earnings multiple for this growth-and-margin combination.
negative_para: A brand-new CEO took charge August 1, 2026, adding real execution/strategy-continuity uncertainty; the sector faces a genuine structural risk from GenAI tools compressing pricing on commoditizable analytics work, and boutique analytics firms of this size typically carry meaningful client-concentration risk we cannot fully quantify from public disclosures. The unusually low quality score also deserves continued monitoring in case it reflects something beyond the capex/cash-deployment explanation we currently favor.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~32x earnings for 21-23% consistent revenue growth and 20%+ margins with a net-cash balance sheet, the multiple is reasonable rather than rich -- ROE (~12% 3-year average) looks unexciting mainly because of a large recent capex/cash deployment (fixed assets 14x higher in one year), not because the core analytics business is capital-inefficient.
